g.text: Approximate locations of Japan's four largest metropolitan areas

text.tspan: Japan is an island nation in East Asia, located in the
northwest Pacific Ocean. It comprises four main islands—
Hokkaido, Honshu, Shikoku, and Kyushu—along with over
6,800 smaller islands. With a population of approximately
125 million, it is one of the world's most densely populated
countries. Japan is renowned for its unique blend of
ancient traditions and cutting-edge technology, stunning
natural landscapes ranging from subtropical to subarctic,
and a rich cultural heritage spanning centuries.

g.text: Japan operates as a parliamentary constitutional monarchy with a highly developed economy and advanced technological infrastructure. As the world's third-largest economy by nominal GDP, it is a global leader in automotive, robotics, and electronics industries.

text.tspan: Japan's economy has experienced notable fluctuations over
the past decade, influenced by global trade dynamics,
currency valuation shifts, and demographic challenges.
Following steady growth from 2015 to 2019, the economy
faced headwinds during the pandemic period and has since
navigated structural adjustments. Despite a gradual decline
in nominal USD terms due to yen depreciation, Japan
remains a dominant economic force in Asia and globally.

g.text: Source: World Bank & IMF estimates (current US$)
The capital offers neon-lit skyscrapers, historic temples, world-class dining, and vibrant neighborhoods like Shibuya and Shinjuku.
Japan's cultural heart features over 2,000 temples and shrines, traditional tea houses, and the stunning Arashiyama bamboo grove.
Known as "Japan's kitchen," Osaka boasts incredible street food, Osaka Castle, and the lively Dotonbori entertainment district.
The Peace Memorial Park and Museum, paired with the iconic floating torii gate on Miyajima Island, create a powerful cultural experience.
Iconic volcanic peaks, natural hot springs (onsen), and scenic lake views offer classic Japanese landscapes and relaxation.
The northernmost island features pristine wilderness, world-class powder skiing, fresh seafood, and the famous Sapporo Snow Festival.

svg.text: Data sources: World Bank, IMF, CIA World Factbook, Japanese Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications. GDP figures in current US$ trillions. Population estimates as of 2024. Infographic compiled for educational purposes.
